page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD processor architecture, this instance features 24 dedicated virtual CPUs provisioned with a total of 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include hardware accelerators or GPUs.

The instance includes 5669 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations for external volumes. The configuration represents a constrained-core variant of the 96 vCPU host chassis, designed specifically to deliver large memory pools and high storage capacity without the overhead of excess compute cores.

From a cost efficiency and architectural tradeoff perspective, the constrained core count enables organizations to optimize per-core software licensing expenses while retaining access to the full memory capacity and high-performance local disk of a larger host. This hardware profile is appropriate for memory-resident relational databases, in-memory caching systems, large-scale data analytics, and enterprise data warehousing workloads that demand high I/O throughput and substantial RAM per process.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on x86_64 AMD processor architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 24 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 672.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high density of 28.0 GB of memory per core. As a constrained-core configuration of a 96-vCPU platform, it maintains access to large physical system resources while limiting active compute units. Local storage consists of a bundled 5669 GB NVMe SSD alongside Premium Storage support, without dedicated GPU acceleration. This architecture offers significant licensing cost efficiency for software billed on a per-core basis, maximizing available memory and I/O capacity per licensed CPU. The instance is suited for enterprise relational database engines, memory-intensive data analytics, in-memory caching clusters, and ETL batch processing pipelines requiring substantial local scratch space.
